Article 20

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons who are legally recognized as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 26.

Article 36
(1) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in Article 35 consists of identification of Victims, legal aid, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, return assistance, or other forms.
(2) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Human Trafficking, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and Women from other vulnerable groups.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent condition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 19
(1) The implementation of Protection for female domestic workers is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhumane treatment, degradation of human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
(2) Female domestic workers as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages, and decent working conditions;
b. health insurance and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 21
(1) The implementation of protection for women former inmates of Correctional Institutions is in order to provide protection from obstacles to adjusting themselves in community life, so that they can carry out life normally.
(2) Women former inmates of Correctional Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
b. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION
Article 32
(1) Women's empowerment and protection is implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on laws and regulations.
(2) In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services shall be established as determined by Regent's Decree.
(3) Women's empowerment and protection shall be coordinated by the Agency handling Women's Empowerment.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children's Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

Article 10
Empowerment of women in the field of education through: a. provision of formal and nonformal education for women in the Region.
b. nonformal education aimed at improving the capabilities of women.
c. nonformal education as referred to in letter b, includes women's empowerment education, skills education and job training.
d. formal and nonformal education as referred to in letter a, shall be regulated by a separate Regional Regulation.

3.10.rationale: In the Indonesian source, there IS explicit economic/livelihood support tied to victims/witnesses within the protection-services chapter. Pasal 35 ayat (1) huruf h states the Regional Government provides “pekerjaan dan penghidupan yang layak …” (decent work and livelihood) as part of protection services for “saksi dan/atau korban” (witnesses and/or victims). This directly links economic support to victims (including women victims of violence, given the surrounding Chapter VII context on protection/recovery of victims of violence against women). The retrieved English candidates included this exact provision ([3.10-65] Article 35(h)), so the judge could have answered Yes but instead focused narrowly on general empowerment provisions. Therefore the main issue is judge reasoning/overly strict interpretation, not missing evidence.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian policy clearly provides measures for women victims/witnesses in the legal process. Pasal 34 ayat (1) huruf e provides “pemberian keterangan pada saat pemeriksaan di sidang pengadilan tanpa bertatap muka dengan tersangka” (giving testimony in court without facing the suspect). Pasal 4 huruf i also grants victims “mendapatkan kemudahan dalam proses peradilan” (facilitation in the judicial process), and Pasal 24 ayat (3) includes “bantuan hukum” (legal aid). These are explicit legal-process protections/services. The retrieved passages contained this information, and the judge’s Yes rationale matches the text. Thus the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.
